title: bls12-381-g1-ecdlp: Cheon d=2^20 with fixed-base windowed BSGS

claims.statement: On bls12-381-g1-ecdlp at n=2^20, with public P0 and A_i=[s^i]P0 for i=1..2^20, T=A_1=[s]P0 and s uniform in [1,r-1], the deterministic Cheon d=2^20 attack described in proof.md recovers s with probability 1 using at most 2^119.891092 total target-group-operation equivalents, W(2^20)=H+R/2000, including all preprocessing, table construction, the 2*sqrt((r-1)/2^20) fixed-base windowed scalar multiplications, hashing, matching, phase 2 and attack-side verification. Peak memory is at most 2^124.807355 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^111.034217 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in total work; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes and every runtime table is included in peak memory. The attack is classical and cold, uses no uncharged advice or quantum steps, and does not amortize work over targets. Correctness is deterministic; the only average-case ingredient, the open-addressing probe count, is charged at a conservative fixed 500 instructions per operation, above its expectation. The exponential memory is required. The bound applies at n=2^20 and any larger n because only the supplied A_d with d=2^20 is used. This is an analytic bound, not a full-size execution, novelty claim or practical break.

experiments.purpose: Exercise the exact two-phase Cheon algebra, fixed-window scalar multiplication, full-point matching and d=2^k recovery on a toy prime-order group, spot-check the production digit structure on boundary and seeded scalars (the no-exception proof is analytic, not experimental), verify the factorization of r-1 and the smallest primitive root, and re-check the production parameters and integer cost ledger. This is evidence only at toy scope, never a production-cost proof.
